summary: beaver-ui-drawer postinstall dropper fetches and executes remote binary
details: The package declares itself as a UI component library but at `npm install` time (via a `postinstall` hook running `node setup.js`) and again when the module is loaded via its `main` entry, it fetches a platform-specific native binary from hardcoded Cloudflare Workers hosts (`oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev`, `.cf100-416.workers.dev`, `.cf101-adf.workers.dev`, `.cf102-baf.workers.dev`, `.cf103-070.workers.dev`) with DNS fallback to `tin.dl.well1.site`, `tina.dl.well1.site`, `ldr.dl.well1.site`, and `win.dl.well1.site`, over paths `/pkg/package`, `/pkg/package-arm64`, `/pkg/loader_mac`, and `/pkg/package.exe`. The downloaded bytes are written to a temp directory, chmod'd 755, and spawned via `child_process`. Both the destination hostnames and the dangerous Node APIs (`child_process`, `chmodSync`, `hostname`, `userInfo`, `platform`, `arch`) are built via string concatenation and array-join to evade static keyword matching. Before the binary is fetched, `installFingerprint()` hashes and transmits host identifiers (`os.hostname()`, `os.userInfo().username`, `process.cwd()`, `process.version`, `process.pid`) as an `installId` to the same Cloudflare Workers infrastructure. The declared UI-components purpose has no legitimate need to run a native executable at install time from obfuscated non-registry hosts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
